date.note: Announcement: a CERN news item dated 25 September 2024 says the result was reported 'at a seminar held at CERN this week'; the seminar day is not given, so the date is recorded to the month. The arXiv preprint (arXiv:2412.12015) was submitted on 16 December 2024 and published as JHEP 02 (2025) 191.
date.quote: At a seminar held at CERN this week, the NA62 collaboration reported the unequivocal confirmation

key_value.note: Branching ratio in units of 10⁻¹¹; the central value is shown as a bare number without a unit.
key_value.quote: Combining NA62 data collected in 2016--2022, a measurement of $B(K^{+}\rightarrow\pi^{+}\nu\bar{\nu}) = \left( 13.0^{+ 3.3}_{- 3.0} \right)\times10^{-11}$ is reported.

key_value_text.quote: Combining NA62 data collected in 2016--2022, a measurement of $B(K^{+}\rightarrow\pi^{+}\nu\bar{\nu}) = \left( 13.0^{+ 3.3}_{- 3.0} \right)\times10^{-11}$ is reported. With $51$ signal candidates observed and an expected background of $18^{+3}_{-2}$ events
key_value_text.value: B(K⁺ → π⁺ ν ν̄) = (13.0+3.3−3.0) × 10⁻¹¹, from 51 signal candidates with an expected background of 18(+3/−2) events, combining data from 2016-2022

name: Observation of the K⁺ → π⁺νν̄ decay and measurement of its branching ratio

significance.note: The abstract gives the significance as 'above 5σ' rather than a precise numeral; the paper's text gives a background-only p-value of 2×10⁻⁷.
significance.quote: the smallest branching ratio measured with a signal significance above 5 sigma

summary.plain: NA62 reports the observation of the very rare kaon decay K⁺→π⁺νν̄ (a positive kaon turning into a pion and two invisible neutrinos), using data from 2016 to 2022: 51 signal candidates over an expected background of 18 events. The paper says this marks the first observation of the decay, at a significance above 5σ.
summary.technical: Observation of K⁺ → π⁺ ν ν̄ (significance above 5σ; background-only p-value 2×10⁻⁷): B(K⁺ → π⁺ ν ν̄) = (13.0+3.3−3.0)×10⁻¹¹ combining 2016-2022 data, including the 2021-2022 data taken at higher beam intensity after modifications to the beamline and detectors; 51 signal candidates with an expected background of 18(+3/−2) events. The paper says the decay becomes the smallest branching ratio measured with a signal significance above 5σ.

title: Observation of the K+ -> pi+ nu nubar decay and measurement of its branching ratio
why_it_matters: The paper's introduction quotes Standard Model branching-ratio predictions of (8.4 ± 1.0)×10⁻¹¹ (from tree-level CKM inputs) and (7.86 ± 0.61)×10⁻¹¹ (from a full CKM parameter fit), with an intrinsic theoretical uncertainty of approximately 3%; the measured branching ratio is (13.0 +3.3 −3.0)×10⁻¹¹.
